title: Verdant on‑prem sync — prep + open actions (scratch)
body:
Context: Verdant is in week 4 of the private deployment engagement. This doc is my personal prep for our weekly sync with Verdant infra + product (Thu 10:00 PT). Populate before call and use as living list for post‑meeting followups.

Meeting objectives (top 3):
- Confirm network peering and BGP staging window (milestone M2).
- Review installer run logs from node pool creation; capture any drift and who will remediate.
- Lock owners for cutover prep tasks (canary traffic, rollback playbook).

Attendees (expected):
- Verdant: Priya Nair (Infra lead), Marco Chen (SRE), Elena Ortiz (Security)
- Redwood: Aisha Malik (Solutions), Ryan Gomez (Deploy eng), Quentin Alvarez (SE)
- Optional: Maya Singh (support for KMS)

Agenda (working):
1) Quick status round — each owner (5m)
2) Network & peering signoff (10m) — Priya/Quentin
3) Installer findings and node health (10m) — Ryan
4) Security checks: egress rules, KMS integration, cert rotation (8m) — Maya/Elena
5) Cutover checklist: canary plan, traffic split, observability guardrails (10m)
6) Blockers and decisions (7m)
7) Next actions + owners (5m)

Milestones / current sprint targets:
- M1: infra baseline + registry image push — DONE (2026-02-22)
- M2: network peering + route tables — target 2026-03-12 (this sync)
- M3: private control plane initial rollout (canary) — target 2026-03-19
- M4: full cutover and SLA handoff — target 2026-03-26

Current blockers (notes / hypotheses):
- Peering: Verdant's network team flagged that CIDR overlap exists between their dev VPC and our management VPC; they proposed NATting — risk: breaks service discovery. Action: propose alternate /22 carve (see options below). Owner: Priya (Verdant), assist: Quentin.
- Installer: two nodes in us‑west‑2 failed kubelet start; logs show libc version mismatch with our base image. Ryan to triage container image tag used by Verdant's bootstrap (possibly pinned to older base).
- KMS: Verdant security needs HSM-backed keys for prod control plane; our default KMS flow is cloud KMS. Maya to map HSM option + gap doc; ETA 3 business days.
- Observability: Prometheus scrape targets missing for model-serving group; consequence: no latency histograms during canary. Need temporary pushgateway or sidecar. Owner: Ryan/Gitlab MR referenced.

Prep notes / items I need to bring:
- Network diagram (attach updated 2026-03-09) — quick screenshot ready.
- Proposed CIDR carve options (A/B/C) with impact table.
- Latest installer logs snippet and node IDs for failed kubelets.
- Canary traffic plan draft (traffic % over time, rollback windows).
- Short checklist for security: KMS model, cert expiry, egress restrictions, audit logging enablement.

Decisions to aim for this meeting:
- Agree on M2 signoff criteria (peering established, route propagation verified, smoke test passed).
- Decide whether to accept NAT workaround (temporary) or require CIDR replan.
- Confirm KMS path for initial canary (cloud KMS vs HSM required for prod).

Open action items (living list) — update status after meeting:
- AI-01: Quentin — share three CIDR carve options + consequences (send to Priya before sync) — DUE 2026-03-11 — status: in_progress
- AI-02: Ryan — collect kubelet logs and open MR to bump base image tag; link to MR in notes — DUE 2026-03-12 — status: in_progress
- AI-03: Maya — draft HSM gap doc and proposed integration flow (include cost estimate) — DUE 2026-03-16 — status: assigned
- AI-04: Aisha — run smoke test checklist on staging once peering done; report pass/fail in thread — DUE 2026-03-12 — status: pending
- AI-05: Priya (Verdant) — confirm network team availability for peering window (copy of maintenance calendar) — DUE 2026-03-11 — status: pending

Notes & talking points (use in sync):
- If Priya pushes NAT as the only option, escalate: express operational limits (service discovery) and propose a temporary port‑mapped proxy for discovery as a last resort with a 2‑week TTL.
- Emphasize rollback: define an explicit rollback point in the cluster snapshot before canary (we need snapshot job ID visible).
- For metrics gap: propose a short term sidecar push (2 days) then schedule proper exporter install.

Risks (short):
- Networking delays will push M3 and M4 by >=1 week, impacting Redwood quarterly onboarding metric for Verdant (FYI for GTM).
- KMS/HSM delays could block prod enablement — escalate to enterprise ops if not resolved by 2026-03-16.

Post-meeting followups (template):
- Send concise meeting note (3 bullets + actions table) within 24 hours.
- Update M2 status in shared runbook page and ping GTM lead if dates slip.
- If CIDR replan chosen, schedule joint planning working session (30m) with Verdant network + Redwood infra.

Scratch / quick calculations:
- Option A: carve /22 from their dev space -> reduces dev subnet by 50% — low ops pain but still viable for short term.
- Option B: reassign small /23 from staging -> minimal overlap but needs migration of 12 VMs (estimate 3 hours co‑ordinated window).
- Option C: use NAT & proxy -> fastest, but increases latency and complicates SRV discovery (operational debt).

Questions I still have (to ask on call):
- Priya: Can you share the exact CIDR list for all Verdant envs (dev/staging/prod)?
- Marco: Who owns cert rotation inside Verdant cluster — do we run cert-manager or they manage?
- Elena: Does Verdant require a formal SCF (security certification form) signed before canary?

Bottom line for the meeting: be concrete — present 2 proposed network fixes, show short term mitigation, and lock owners for KMS decision. Keep tone collaborative but clear on what we cannot accept operationally (no permanent NAT).

End of scratch notes. Update AI list during meeting.

-- Quentin
